questions.q: What does the Fixed Assets Asset Register document?
options: Only the company's cash balances
Tangible assets like buildings, equipment, and vehicles, along with details like acquisition cost, date, category, and location
Unpaid customer invoices
Bank reconciliation status
questions.explain: The Asset Register is the authoritative, detailed listing behind the Fixed Assets line on the Balance Sheet.

questions.q: Why does depreciation reporting matter on both the Balance Sheet and the Income Statement?
options: It has no effect on either statement
It reduces an asset's net book value on the Balance Sheet while also posting as a depreciation expense that reduces Net Income on the Income Statement
It only affects the Trial Balance, never the two main statements
It is purely a Cash Management concept
questions.explain: Depreciation simultaneously reduces the Balance Sheet's asset value and appears as an expense reducing Net Income on the Income Statement.

questions.q: What is the core activity behind Cash Management's reporting job?
options: Tracking depreciation of fixed assets
Bank statement reconciliation — comparing Oracle Fusion's recorded transactions against the bank's own statement
Generating customer statements
Scheduling BI Publisher reports
questions.explain: Cash Management's reporting centers on reconciling the system's recorded cash position to what the bank itself reports.

questions.q: What is an example of an item that might surface as unmatched during bank statement reconciliation?
options: A check that has not yet cleared the bank
An asset acquisition date
An OTBI subject area
A Smart View shared connection
questions.explain: Timing differences like an uncleared check, or items like an unrecorded bank fee, are typical items surfaced during reconciliation.

questions.q: What common pattern do Fixed Assets and Cash Management reports share with other reports covered in this chapter?
options: Neither report type connects to any financial statement
A summarized line on a formal financial statement is only as trustworthy as the detailed, module-specific report supporting it
Both are built exclusively using OTBI, never BI Publisher or Financial Reporting Studio
Neither module's reports are reviewed during close
questions.explain: This chapter's recurring theme is that formal statement lines (Fixed Assets, Cash) depend on detailed supporting reports (Asset Register, bank reconciliation) being accurate first.
